chenmi-1916.summary: Four telegrams from Tokyo to the Hunanese group's address in Shanghai (ヒツキン, 277 Avenue Joffre): Shandong and Bo Wenwei; the joint telegram to Li Yuanhong, Cen Chunxuan and the provinces; an elite division under Zhao Hengti for Li Yuanhong; 300 yuan for Jiang Fangzhen.
chenmi-1916.en:
Please pass on to brother Liewu: if, on the Shandong side, they want you to take charge of unifying matters, you may accept directly; ask Puquan (Zhang Ji) to go with you. From here we will help with all our strength. What do you think? Awaiting your reply. Xing.

Note: Read as a blind check: not used to find the key. Digits re-read by Brice Dudout.

To the three brothers Xiao, Yong and Feng: the telegram to Li [Yuanhong], Cen [Chunxuan] and the provinces is very hard to word. If our positions are not unanimous, we risk looking divided; if we write as your telegram says, people will see it as opportunism. Please obtain the agreement of the National Protection Army and have the draft written and sent from your side. Japan’s attitude is very much wait-and-see; the comrades in Shanghai should take a firm stand, and the Military Council above all must be clear.

snip.cap: N16, first sheet, 10 June 1916: the 辰密 prefix 6591 1378 and the digit grid in kanji numerals, addressed to ヒツキン, Shanghai.
snip.credit: Diplomatic Archives of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan, JACAR B03050089300, PDF p. 11 (left), via Brice Dudout’s wenmi repository

system: The Chinese telegraph code (明密 book) with its pages, columns and rows renumbered by hand for the 辰密 correspondent (S. Tomokiyo); equivalently key C92 as a formula (key.md).
